sanskrit: na tat puruṣakāreṇa na ca daivena kena cit sukham eṣyati tat tasya yad evaṃ saṃyatātmanaḥ
english: Neither by human effort nor by any working of fate does such happiness come to a man—that happiness belongs only to him whose self is thus restrained.

sanskrit: sukhena tena saṃyukto raṃsyate dhyānakarmaṇi gacchanti yogino hy evaṃ nirvāṇaṃ tan nirāmayam
english: United with that happiness, he delights in the labor of meditation; for thus the yogins go to that nirvāṇa which is free from all affliction.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca cāturāśramyam uktaṃ te rājadharmās tathaiva ca nānāśrayāś ca bahava itihāsāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have expounded the four stages of life and likewise the duties of kings, and many ancient narratives of diverse kinds, resting on various themes.

sanskrit: śrutās tvattaḥ kathāś caiva dharmayuktā mahāmate saṃdeho 'sti tu kaś cin me tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: From you, O great-minded one, I have heard discourses joined with dharma; yet one doubt remains in me, and you should resolve it.

sanskrit: jāpakānāṃ phalāvāptiṃ śrotum icchāmi bhārata kiṃ phalaṃ japatām uktaṃ kva vā tiṣṭhanti jāpakāḥ
english: I wish to hear, O descendant of Bharata, the reward attained by those who practice recitation. What fruit is declared for those who murmur the sacred words, and in what abode do such reciters dwell?

sanskrit: japasya ca vidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ vaktum arhasi me 'nagha jāpakā iti kiṃ caitat sāṃkhyayogakriyāvidhiḥ
english: And you should tell me, O blameless one, the whole rule of recitation. What is this matter of the reciters—is it the practice of Sāṃkhya, or of Yoga, or of ritual action?

sanskrit: kiṃ yajñavidhir evaiṣa kim etaj japyam ucyate etan me sarvam ācakṣva sarvajño hy asi me mataḥ
english: Is this merely a rite of sacrifice, or what is it that is called the muttered prayer? Declare all this to me, for in my judgment you are the knower of all things.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yamasya yat purā vṛttaṃ kālasya brāhmaṇasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they relate an ancient tale—what once befell of old between Yama, and Kāla, and a certain brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsa eva vedānte vartate japanaṃ prati vedavādābhinirvṛttā śāntir brahmaṇy avasthitau mārgau tāv apy ubhāv etau saṃśritau na ca saṃśritau
english: In the Vedānta, renunciation alone governs the practice of recitation; the peace that arises from the teaching of the Vedas rests in Brahman. Both these paths abide there—and yet are not so wholly abiding.

sanskrit: yathā saṃśrūyate rājan kāraṇaṃ cātra vakṣyate manaḥsamādhir atrāpi tathendriyajayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: As it is heard among men, O king, so the reason shall be set forth here; and herein concentration of the mind, as also the conquest of the senses, is taught.

sanskrit: satyam agniparīcāro viviktānāṃ ca sevanam dhyānaṃ tapo damaḥ kṣāntir anasūyā mitāśanam
english: Truthfulness, the tending of the sacred fire, the frequenting of solitary places, meditation, austerity, self-restraint, patience, freedom from envy, and moderate eating—

sanskrit: viṣayapratisaṃhāro mitajalpas tathā śamaḥ eṣa pravṛttako dharmo nivṛttakam atho śṛṇu
english: the withdrawal from objects of sense, sparing speech, and tranquility—this is the dharma of active engagement; now hear of the dharma of withdrawal.

sanskrit: yathā nivartate karma japato brahmacāriṇaḥ etat sarvam aśeṣeṇa yathoktaṃ parivarjayet trividhaṃ mārgam āsādya vyaktāvyaktam anāśrayam
english: As action ceases for the celibate who practices recitation, so should he abandon all this without remainder, just as it has been taught, having reached the threefold path—the manifest, the unmanifest, and that which has no support.

sanskrit: kuśoccayaniṣaṇṇaḥ san kuśahastaḥ kuśaiḥ śikhī cīraiḥ parivṛtas tasmin madhye channaḥ kuśais tathā
english: Seated upon a heap of kuśa grass, kuśa in hand, his crown of hair bound with kuśa, wrapped in bark garments, and there in the midst veiled about with kuśa—

sanskrit: viṣayebhyo namaskuryād viṣayān na ca bhāvayet sāmyam utpādya manaso manasy eva mano dadhat
english: he should make obeisance to the objects of sense yet dwell upon them no longer; having brought the mind to evenness, he should set the mind upon the mind alone.

sanskrit: tad dhiyā dhyāyati brahma japan vai saṃhitāṃ hitām saṃnyasyaty atha vā tāṃ vai samādhau paryavasthitaḥ
english: With the intellect he meditates upon Brahman, murmuring the salutary sacred text; or else, established in deep absorption, he lays even that text aside.

sanskrit: dhyānam utpādayaty atra saṃhitābalasaṃśrayāt śuddhātmā tapasā dānto nivṛttadveṣakāmavān
english: Here he generates meditation through the support and power of the sacred text—pure of self, subdued by austerity, freed from hatred and desire,

sanskrit: arāgamoho nirdvaṃdvo na śocati na sajjate na kartākaraṇīyānāṃ na kāryāṇām iti sthitiḥ
english: without passion or delusion, beyond the pairs of opposites, he neither grieves nor clings; he is no doer of deeds that ought not to be done, nor of deeds that ought—such is his abiding.

sanskrit: na cāhaṃkārayogena manaḥ prasthāpayet kva cit na cātmagrahaṇe yukto nāvamānī na cākriyaḥ
english: He should never set the mind in motion through the working of egoism, nor be intent upon grasping at the self; he is neither contemptuous nor wholly inactive.

sanskrit: dhyānakriyāparo yukto dhyānavān dhyānaniścayaḥ dhyāne samādhim utpādya tad api tyajati kramāt
english: Devoted to the practice of meditation, disciplined, full of meditation, resolute in meditation, having generated deep absorption within meditation, he by degrees relinquishes even that.

sanskrit: sa vai tasyām avasthāyāṃ sarvatyāgakṛtaḥ sukhī nirīhas tyajati prāṇān brāhmīṃ saṃśrayate tanum
english: In that very state, having renounced all things, happy and without striving, he gives up his vital breaths and takes refuge in the body of Brahman.

sanskrit: atha vā necchate tatra brahmakāyaniṣevaṇam utkrāmati ca mārgastho naiva kva cana jāyate
english: Or else, if he desires not the dwelling in the body of Brahman, he ascends, abiding on the path, and is born no more anywhere at all.

sanskrit: ātmabuddhiṃ samāsthāya śāntībhūto nirāmayaḥ amṛtaṃ virajaḥśuddham ātmānaṃ pratipadyate
english: Established in the knowledge of the Self, become tranquil and free from affliction, he attains the Self—immortal, stainless, and pure.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gatīnām uttamā prāptiḥ kathitā jāpakeṣv iha ekaivaiṣā gatis teṣām uta yānty aparām api
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The highest of attainments among destinies has been told for the reciters here. Is this their one and only goal, or do they go to another as well?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājañ jāpakānāṃ gatiṃ vibho yathā gacchanti nirayam anekaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Bhīṣma said: Listen attentively, O king and lord, to the destiny of the reciters, how they go to many a hell, O bull among men.

sanskrit: yathoktam etat pūrvaṃ yo nānutiṣṭhati jāpakaḥ ekadeśakriyaś cātra nirayaṃ sa nigacchati
english: The reciter who does not perform this as it was taught before, but practices it only in part, descends here into hell.

sanskrit: avajñānena kurute na tuṣyati na śocati īdṛśo jāpako yāti nirayaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: He who performs it with contempt, who feels neither contentment nor remorse—such a reciter goes to hell; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārakṛtaś caiva sarve nirayagāminaḥ parāvamānī puruṣo bhavitā nirayopagaḥ
english: And all who are made of egoism are bound for hell; the man who despises others shall become one who descends into hell.

sanskrit: abhidhyāpūrvakaṃ japyaṃ kurute yaś ca mohitaḥ yatrābhidhyāṃ sa kurute taṃ vai nirayam ṛcchati
english: He who, deluded, performs his recitation with covetous longing—wherever he directs that longing, to that very hell he comes.

sanskrit: athaiśvaryapravṛttaḥ sañ jāpakas tatra rajyate sa eva nirayas tasya nāsau tasmāt pramucyate
english: And the reciter who turns toward lordly power takes delight therein; that very thing becomes his hell, and from it he is not released.

sanskrit: rāgeṇa jāpako japyaṃ kurute tatra mohitaḥ yatrāsya rāgaḥ patati tatra tatropajāyate
english: The reciter who, deluded, performs his recitation out of passion—wherever his passion falls, there and there again he is born.

sanskrit: durbuddhir akṛtaprajñaś cale manasi tiṣṭhati calām eva gatiṃ yāti nirayaṃ vādhigacchati
english: The man of evil mind, his wisdom unformed, who abides in a wavering mind, goes to a wavering destiny, or else attains hell.

sanskrit: akṛtaprajñako bālo mohaṃ gacchati jāpakaḥ sa mohān nirayaṃ yāti tatra gatvānuśocati
english: The reciter who is a fool, his wisdom unformed, falls into delusion; through that delusion he goes to hell, and having gone there, he grieves.

sanskrit: dṛḍhagrāhī karomīti japyaṃ japati jāpakaḥ na saṃpūrṇo na vā yukto nirayaṃ so 'dhigacchati
english: The reciter who, clinging stubbornly with the thought "I am the doer," murmurs his prayer—neither perfected nor disciplined—attains hell.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca animittaṃ paraṃ yat tad avyaktaṃ brahmaṇi sthitam sadbhūto jāpakaḥ kasmāt sa śarīram athāviśet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That supreme, causeless, unmanifest reality abides in Brahman; the reciter who has become real—why then should he enter a body again?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca duṣprajñānena nirayā bahavaḥ samudāhṛtāḥ praśastaṃ jāpakatvaṃ ca doṣāś caite tadātmakāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Through false understanding many hells have been declared; the office of the reciter is praiseworthy, yet these faults belong to its very nature when misused.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kīdṛśo jāpako yāti nirayaṃ varṇayasva me kautūhalaṃ hi me jātaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What manner of reciter goes to hell? Describe this to me, for curiosity has arisen in me, and you should tell it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dharmasyāṃśaḥ prasūto 'si dharmiṣṭho 'si svabhāvataḥ dharmamūlāśrayaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣvāvahito 'nagha
english: Bhīṣma said: You are born as a portion of Dharma, and by your very nature you are most righteous; listen attentively, O blameless one, to a discourse whose root and refuge is dharma.

sanskrit: amūni yāni sthānāni devānāṃ paramātmanām nānāsaṃsthānavarṇāni nānārūpaphalāni ca
english: Those abodes yonder of the gods, the supreme-souled ones, of manifold forms and colors and of manifold shapes and fruits—

sanskrit: divyāni kāmacārīṇi vimānāni sabhās tathā ākrīḍā vividhā rājan padminyaś cāmalodakāḥ
english: the celestial palaces that move at will, and the assembly halls, and the varied pleasure-gardens, O king, and the lotus-ponds of unsullied waters—

sanskrit: caturṇāṃ lokapālānāṃ śukrasyātha bṛhaspateḥ marutāṃ viśvadevānāṃ sādhyānām aśvinor api
english: the abodes of the four guardians of the worlds, of Śukra and of Bṛhaspati, of the Maruts, the Viśvadevas, the Sādhyas, and the Aśvins as well,

sanskrit: rudrādityavasūnāṃ ca tathānyeṣāṃ divaukasām ete vai nirayās tāta sthānasya paramātmanaḥ
english: and of the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the other dwellers in heaven—all these, my son, are but hells compared with the abode of the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ cānimittaṃ ca na ca kleśabhayāvṛtam dvābhyāṃ muktaṃ tribhir muktam aṣṭābhis tribhir eva ca
english: That state is free from fear and without cause, not enveloped in the dread of affliction—freed from the two, freed from the three, from the eight and again from the three.

sanskrit: caturlakṣaṇavarjaṃ tu catuṣkāraṇavarjitam apraharṣam anānandam aśokaṃ vigataklamam
english: It is devoid of the four marks and free from the four causes, without elation, without rejoicing, without sorrow, its weariness wholly gone.

sanskrit: kālaḥ saṃpacyate tatra na kālas tatra vai prabhuḥ sa kālasya prabhū rājan svargasyāpi tatheśvaraḥ
english: There Time itself is ripened; there Time holds no dominion. That Self, O king, is the lord of Time and likewise the ruler even of heaven.

sanskrit: ātmakevalatāṃ prāptas tatra gatvā na śocati īdṛśaṃ paramaṃ sthānaṃ nirayās te ca tādṛśāḥ
english: Having reached the absolute aloneness of the Self and gone there, one grieves no more. Such is that supreme abode, and such are those hells beside it.

sanskrit: ete te nirayāḥ proktāḥ sarva eva yathātatham tasya sthānavarasyeha sarve nirayasaṃjñitāḥ
english: All these hells have been declared to you exactly as they are; compared with that highest abode here, all are reckoned as hells.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kālamṛtyuyamānāṃ ca brāhmaṇasya ca sattama vivādo vyāhṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The dispute among Kāla, Mṛtyu, and Yama, and the brāhmaṇa, O most excellent one, was mentioned before; you should now relate it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ikṣvākoḥ sūryaputrasya yad vṛttaṃ brāhmaṇasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they relate an ancient tale—what befell Ikṣvāku, the son of the Sun, and a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kālasya mṛtyoś ca tathā yad vṛttaṃ tan nibodha me yathā sa teṣāṃ saṃvādo yasmin sthāne 'pi cābhavat
english: And of Kāla and Mṛtyu likewise—learn from me what befell them: how that converse of theirs came about, and in what place it took place.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo jāpakaḥ kaś cid dharmavṛtto mahāyaśāḥ ṣaḍaṅgavin mahāprājñaḥ paippalādiḥ sa kauśikaḥ
english: There was a certain brāhmaṇa, a reciter, of righteous conduct and great renown, knower of the six Vedāṅgas, exceedingly wise—a Kauśika of the Paippalāda line.

sanskrit: tasyāparokṣaṃ vijñānaṃ ṣaḍaṅgeṣu tathaiva ca vedeṣu caiva niṣṇāto himavatpādasaṃśrayaḥ
english: His knowledge of the six Vedāṅgas was direct and immediate, and he was deeply versed in the Vedas as well; he dwelt at the foot of the Himālaya.

sanskrit: so 'ntyaṃ brāhmaṃ tapas tepe saṃhitāṃ saṃyato japan tasya varṣasahasraṃ tu niyamena tathā gatam
english: He performed the supreme austerity proper to Brahman, restrained, murmuring the sacred text; and so a thousand years passed for him under that vow.

sanskrit: sa devyā darśitaḥ sākṣāt prītāsmīti tadā kila japyam āvartayaṃs tūṣṇīṃ na ca tāṃ kiṃ cid abravīt
english: To him the Goddess showed herself in person, saying, "I am pleased"; yet he, still murmuring his recitation, kept silent and said nothing to her at all.

sanskrit: tasyānukampayā devī prītā samabhavat tadā vedamātā tatas tasya taj japyaṃ samapūjayat
english: Out of compassion for him the Goddess became gladdened then; and so the Mother of the Vedas honored that recitation of his.

sanskrit: samāptajapyas tūtthāya śirasā pādayos tathā papāta devyā dharmātmā vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then, his recitation completed, the righteous-souled one rose and bowed his head at the feet of the Goddess, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā devi prasannā tvaṃ darśanaṃ cāgatā mama yadi vāpi prasannāsi japye me ramatāṃ manaḥ
english: "By good fortune, O Goddess, you are gracious to me and have come into my sight; and if indeed you are pleased, let my mind delight in recitation."

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca kiṃ prārthayasi viprarṣe kiṃ ceṣṭaṃ karavāṇi te prabrūhi japatāṃ śreṣṭha sarvaṃ tat te bhaviṣyati
english: Sāvitrī said: What do you seek, O sage among brāhmaṇas? What desired thing shall I do for you? Speak, O best of those who recite, and all that shall be yours.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā devyā vipraḥ provāca dharmavit japyaṃ prati mameccheyaṃ vardhatv iti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by the Goddess, the brāhmaṇa, knower of dharma, then said: "Let my desire toward recitation grow stronger again and again.

sanskrit: manasaś ca samādhir me vardhetāhar ahaḥ śubhe tat tatheti tato devī madhuraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: And may the concentration of my mind increase day by day, O auspicious one." "So be it," the Goddess then answered him sweetly.

sanskrit: idaṃ caivāparaṃ prāha devī tatpriyakāmyayā nirayaṃ naiva yātāsi yatra yātā dvijarṣabhāḥ
english: And the Goddess, wishing to do him a further kindness, spoke this besides: "You shall never go to that hell to which other bulls among the twice-born have gone.

sanskrit: yāsyasi brahmaṇaḥ sthānam animittam aninditam sādhaye bhavitā caitad yat tvayāham ihārthitā
english: You shall go to the abode of Brahman—the causeless, the blameless. I shall accomplish this, since you have entreated me here."

sanskrit: niyato japa caikāgro dharmas tvāṃ samupaiṣyati kālo mṛtyur yamaś caiva samāyāsyanti te 'ntikam bhavitā ca vivādo 'tra tava teṣāṃ ca dharmataḥ
english: "Recite, restrained and single-minded, and Dharma will come to you. Kāla, Mṛtyu, and Yama too shall come into your presence, and there shall be a dispute, in accordance with dharma, between you and them."

sanskrit: evam uktvā bhagavatī jagāma bhavanaṃ svakam brāhmaṇo 'pi japann āste divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ tadā
english: Having spoken thus, the blessed Goddess went to her own abode; and the brāhmaṇa too remained reciting then for a celestial hundred years.

sanskrit: samāpte niyame tasminn atha viprasya dhīmataḥ sākṣāt prītas tadā dharmo darśayām āsa taṃ dvijam
english: When that vow of the wise brāhmaṇa was completed, Dharma, well pleased, then showed himself in person to that twice-born one.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca dvijāte paśya māṃ dharmam ahaṃ tvāṃ draṣṭum āgataḥ japyasya ca phalaṃ yat te saṃprāptaṃ tac ca me śṛṇu
english: Dharma said: O twice-born one, behold me—I am Dharma, come to look upon you. Hear from me too what fruit of recitation you have attained.

sanskrit: jitā lokās tvayā sarve ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ devānāṃ nirayān sādho sarvān utkramya yāsyasi
english: All the worlds have been won by you, both the celestial and the human; transcending all the hells of the gods, O virtuous one, you shall go beyond.

sanskrit: prāṇatyāgaṃ kuru mune gaccha lokān yathepsitān tyaktvātmanaḥ śarīraṃ ca tato lokān avāpsyasi
english: Give up your vital breaths, O sage, and go to the worlds you desire; abandoning your own body, you shall then attain those worlds.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kṛtaṃ lokair hi me dharma gaccha ca tvaṃ yathāsukham bahuduḥkhasukhaṃ dehaṃ notsṛjeyam ahaṃ vibho
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Enough of the worlds for me, O Dharma; go you wherever you please. I will not cast off this body, lord, with all its many sorrows and joys.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca avaśyaṃ bhoḥ śarīraṃ te tyaktavyaṃ munipuṃgava svarga ārohyatāṃ vipra kiṃ vā te rocate 'nagha
english: Dharma said: Inevitably, sir, your body must be relinquished, O bull among sages. Let heaven be ascended, O brāhmaṇa—or what else, O blameless one, is your pleasure?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca na rocaye svargavāsaṃ vinā dehād ahaṃ vibho gaccha dharma na me śraddhā svargaṃ gantuṃ vinātmanā
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I take no pleasure in dwelling in heaven apart from this body, lord. Go, Dharma; I have no wish to go to heaven without my own self.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca alaṃ dehe manaḥ kṛtvā tyaktvā dehaṃ sukhī bhava gaccha lokān arajaso yatra gatvā na śocasi
english: Dharma said: Cease to set your mind upon the body; cast off the body and be happy. Go to the stainless worlds, where, once gone, you grieve no more.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca rame japan mahābhāga kṛtaṃ lokaiḥ sanātanaiḥ saśarīreṇa gantavyo mayā svargo na vā vibho
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I delight in reciting, O illustrious one; enough of the eternal worlds. Either I shall go to heaven with my body, lord, or not at all.

sanskrit: dharma uvāca yadi tvaṃ necchasi tyaktuṃ śarīraṃ paśya vai dvija eṣa kālas tathā mṛtyur yamaś ca tvām upāgatāḥ
english: Dharma said: If you do not wish to give up your body, then behold, O twice-born one—here are Kāla, and Mṛtyu, and Yama, come to you.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha vaivasvataḥ kālo mṛtyuś ca tritayaṃ vibho brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ mahābhāgam upāgamyedam abruvan
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the son of Vivasvat, and Kāla, and Mṛtyu—these three, O lord—approaching that illustrious brāhmaṇa, spoke thus:

sanskrit: tapaso 'sya sutaptasya tathā sucaritasya ca phalaprāptis tava śreṣṭhā yamo 'haṃ tvām upabruve
english: "Of this austerity, well performed and well conducted, the attainment of fruit is supreme for you. I am Yama, and I speak to you.

sanskrit: yathāvad asya japyasya phalaṃ prāptas tvam uttamam kālas te svargam āroḍhuṃ kālo 'haṃ tvām upāgataḥ
english: Duly have you attained the highest fruit of this recitation; the time has come for you to ascend to heaven. I am Kāla, and I have come to you.

sanskrit: mṛtyuṃ mā viddhi dharmajña rūpiṇaṃ svayam āgatam kālena coditaṃ vipra tvām ito netum adya vai
english: Know me to be Mṛtyu, O knower of dharma, come in person in embodied form, urged on by Kāla, O brāhmaṇa, to lead you hence this very day."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca svāgataṃ sūryaputrāya kālāya ca mahātmane mṛtyave cātha dharmāya kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇi vaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Welcome to the son of the Sun, and to the great-souled Kāla, and to Mṛtyu, and to Dharma. What service shall I render you?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca arghyaṃ pādyaṃ ca dattvā sa tebhyas tatra samāgame abravīt paramaprītaḥ svaśaktyā kiṃ karomi vaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having offered them the welcome-water and water for the feet at that meeting, he, exceedingly pleased, said: "By my own power, what may I do for you?"
